newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi rejects Burma government charge on unrest.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi rejects Burma government charge on unrest.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Monday rejected as "absolutely ridiculous" the government's accusation that some members of her National League for Democracy (NLD) party were behind the latest student unrest.
"This is absolutely ridiculous. They should be prepared to deal with their problems instead of trying to find someone else to blame," she told Reuters by telephone.

She was reacting to a statement by a government spokesmen that some members of her NLD, elements of the outlawed Burma Communist Party and student exiles of the All Burma Students' Democratic Front were behind the unrest.

"They are never prepared to accept their responsibility as a government. This theory of conspiracy is totally out of date. We want some more modern approach (to deal with the problems)," Suu Kyi said.
University student protesters, who last week staged two major street demonstrations, and Suu Kyi have denied any links.

Yangon University and the Yangon Institute of Technology students held a protest last Monday and Tuesday and another one on Saturday to denounce alleged police brutality and to seek greater freedoms. The government broke up the protests, detained hundreds of students briefly and later freed them.
